claim: CENP-A is a histone H3 variant that is a key epigenetic determinant of centromeres.
source: Centromere protein (CENP) A, a histone H3 variant, is a key epigenetic determinant of chromosome domains known as centromeres.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by established scientific knowledge about CENP-A's role in centromere specification.

claim: Centromeres nucleate kinetochores, which are multi-subunit complexes that capture spindle microtubules to promote chromosome segregation during mitosis.
source: Centromeres nucleate kinetochores, multi-subunit complexes that capture spindle microtubules to promote chromosome segregation during mitosis.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and represents established knowledge about kinetochore function.

claim: CENP-C and CENP-N are two kinetochore proteins that recognize CENP-A in the context of a rare CENP-A nucleosome.
source: Two kinetochore proteins, CENP-C and CENP-N, recognize CENP-A in the context of a rare CENP-A nucleosome.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to previous work throughout the manuscript.

claim: CENP-N uses charge and space complementarity to decode the L1 loop that is unique to CENP-A.
source: CENP-N uses charge and space complementarity to decode the L1 loop that is unique to CENP-A.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CENP-N engages in extensive interactions with a 15-base pair segment of the distorted nucleosomal DNA double helix.
source: It also engages in extensive interactions with a 15-base pair segment of the distorted nucleosomal DNA double helix, in a position predicted to exclude chromatin remodelling enzymes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by structural data from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: The position of CENP-N binding on the nucleosome is predicted to exclude chromatin remodelling enzymes.
source: It also engages in extensive interactions with a 15-base pair segment of the distorted nucleosomal DNA double helix, in a position predicted to exclude chromatin remodelling enzymes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and represents an inference based on the structural data and comparison with chromatin remodeler binding sites.

claim: Stable centromere recruitment of CENP-N requires a coincident interaction with a newly identified binding motif on nucleosome-bound CENP-C, in addition to CENP-A.
source: Besides CENP-A, stable centromere recruitment of CENP-N requires a coincident interaction with a newly identified binding motif on nucleosome-bound CENP-C.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by biochemical and cellular data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Accurate segregation of chromosomes during cell division is a prerequisite for healthy cell physiology and transmission of genetic information across generations.
source: Accurate segregation of chromosomes from a mother cell to its two daughters during cell division is a prerequisite for healthy cell physiology and for the transmission of the genetic information across generations (Santaguida and Amon, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Specialized, conserved molecular machinery dedicated to chromosome segregation has been identified in the majority of eukaryotic organisms studied to date.
source: Specialized, conserved molecular machinery dedicated to this crucial function has been identified in the majority of eukaryotic organisms studied to date (Drinnenberg et al., 2016; van Hooff et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The defining mark of centromeres in almost all known eukaryotes is the enrichment of CENP-A, which replaces histone H3 in nucleosomes.
source: A crucial role in this process is played by centromeres, specialized chromatin domains whose defining mark in almost all known eukaryotes is the enrichment of centromeric protein A (CENP-A, also known as CenH3), which replaces histone H3 in nucleosomes (Fukagawa and Earnshaw, 2014; Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The primary function of centromeres is to provide a platform for the assembly of kinetochores.
source: The primary function of centromeres is to provide a platform for the assembly of macromolecular complexes known as kinetochores, whose task in turn is the physical capture of microtubules of the mitotic spindle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about centromere function.

claim: Kinetochores contain approximately 30 core subunits.
source: Kinetochores contain approximately 30 core subunits, normally subdivided in centromere-proximal and microtubule-proximal groups.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about kinetochore composition.

claim: The microtubule-proximal subunits of the kinetochore are collectively denoted as the KMN assembly.
source: The microtubule-proximal subunits (outer kinetochore), which are directly implicated in microtubule binding, are usually denoted as the KMN assembly, from the name of three sub-complexes, the Knl1, Mis12, and Ndc80 complexes (Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The centromere-proximal subunits of the kinetochore are collectively identified as the constitutive centromere associated network (CCAN).
source: The centromere-proximal subunits (inner kinetochore), which are also organized in sub-complexes, are collectively identified as the constitutive centromere associated network (CCAN) because they appear to reside at centromeres for the entire cell cycle (Cheeseman and Desai, 2008; Foltz et al., 2006; Izuta et al., 2006; Obuse et al., 2004; Okada et al., 2006)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CENP-A nucleosomes interact specifically and selectively with two CCAN components, CENP-C and CENP-N, in vitro.
source: In vitro, these interact specifically and selectively with two CCAN components, CENP-C and CENP-N (Carroll et al., 2010, 2009; Guo et al., 2017; Guse et al., 2011; Hoffmann et al., 2016; Klare et al., 2015; Nagpal et al., 2015; Samejima et al., 2015; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Binding of CENP-C and CENP-N to CENP-A nucleosomes requires two regions where the CENP-A sequence diverges significantly from that of histone H3: the L1 loop and the C-terminal tail.
source: Binding of these proteins to CENP-A nucleosomes has been shown to require two regions where the CENP-A sequence diverges significantly from that of histone H3, the L1 loop and the C-terminal tail (Carroll et al., 2009; Fachinetti et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2017; Kato et al., 2013; Logsdon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: An evolutionary conserved motif of CENP-C is sufficient for recognition of CENP-A in vitro.
source: An evolutionary conserved motif of CENP-C, present in one or two copies in different organisms, is sufficient for recognition of CENP-A in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents knowledge from previous studies.

claim: The CENP-C motif interacts primarily with a solvent-exposed acidic patch on the H2A and H2B subunits of the CENP-A nucleosome and also decodes the divergent C-terminal tail of CENP-A.
source: This motif interacts primarily with a solvent-exposed acidic patch on the H2A and H2B subunits of the CENP-A nucleosome and also decodes the divergent C-terminal tail of CENP-A (Guo et al., 2017; Kato et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Human CENP-C has two copies of the CENP-A recognition motif, referred to as the central motif and the CENP-C motif.
source: The two copies of this motif in human CENP-C are referred to as the central motif (or domain) and the CENP-C motif (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents established knowledge about CENP-C structure.

claim: The central motif of CENP-C is required for efficient centromere retention of newly incorporated CENP-A.
source: While at least the central motif has been shown to be required for efficient centromere retention of newly incorporated CENP-A (Guo et al., 2017), neither motif appears to be strictly necessary for centromere localization of CENP-C in human cells (Guo et al., 2017), likely because CENP-C contains binding sites for additional CCAN subunits that can stabilize its centromere localization even in the absence of a direct interaction with CENP-A (Guo et al., 2017; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2013; Klare et al., 2015; McKinley et al., 2015; Nagpal et al., 2015; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Neither the central motif nor the CENP-C motif appears to be strictly necessary for centromere localization of CENP-C in human cells.
source: While at least the central motif has been shown to be required for efficient centromere retention of newly incorporated CENP-A (Guo et al., 2017), neither motif appears to be strictly necessary for centromere localization of CENP-C in human cells (Guo et al., 2017), likely because CENP-C contains binding sites for additional CCAN subunits that can stabilize its centromere localization even in the absence of a direct interaction with CENP-A (Guo et al., 2017; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2013; Klare et al., 2015; McKinley et al., 2015; Nagpal et al., 2015; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CENP-C contains binding sites for additional CCAN subunits that can stabilize its centromere localization even in the absence of a direct interaction with CENP-A.
source: While at least the central motif has been shown to be required for efficient centromere retention of newly incorporated CENP-A (Guo et al., 2017), neither motif appears to be strictly necessary for centromere localization of CENP-C in human cells (Guo et al., 2017), likely because CENP-C contains binding sites for additional CCAN subunits that can stabilize its centromere localization even in the absence of a direct interaction with CENP-A (Guo et al., 2017; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2013; Klare et al., 2015; McKinley et al., 2015; Nagpal et al., 2015; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CENP-C acts as a blueprint in the establishment of the inner to outer kinetochore axis.
source: The specific succession of binding sites within CENP-C, a protein that secondary structure prediction algorithms identify as being largely intrinsically disordered, has led to suggest that it acts as a blueprint in the establishment of the inner to outer kinetochore axis, with an N-terminal motif involved in stabilizing the outer kinetochore, a middle region involved in stabilizing the inner kinetochore CCAN complex, and a C-terminal region involved in interactions with the centromeric chromatin (Figure 1A) (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Kato et al., 2013; Klare et al., 2015; McKinley et al., 2015; Przewloka et al., 2011; Screpanti et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CENP-C is largely intrinsically disordered according to secondary structure prediction algorithms.
source: The specific succession of binding sites within CENP-C, a protein that secondary structure prediction algorithms identify as being largely intrinsically disordered, has led to suggest that it acts as a blueprint in the establishment of the inner to outer kinetochore axis, with an N-terminal motif involved in stabilizing the outer kinetochore, a middle region involved in stabilizing the inner kinetochore CCAN complex, and a C-terminal region involved in interactions with the centromeric chromatin (Figure 1A) (Gascoigne et al., 2011; Kato et al., 2013; Klare et al., 2015; McKinley et al., 2015; Przewloka et al., 2011; Screpanti et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and represents a prediction based on computational analysis.

claim: CENP-N forms a constitutive complex with CENP-L.
source: CENP-N forms a constitutive complex with CENP-L (designated CENP-LN complex), which in turn interacts with the CENP-HIKM complex and with CENP-C (Guo et al., 2017; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2013; Klare et al., 2015; McKinley et al., 2015; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The CENP-LN complex interacts with the CENP-HIKM complex and with CENP-C.
source: CENP-N forms a constitutive complex with CENP-L (designated CENP-LN complex), which in turn interacts with the CENP-HIKM complex and with CENP-C (Guo et al., 2017; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2013; Klare et al., 2015; McKinley et al., 2015; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Binding of CENP-N requires the exposed L1 loop of CENP-A and may also reach into the neighboring DNA.
source: Binding of CENP-N requires the exposed L1 loop of CENP-A and may also reach into the neighboring DNA (Carroll et al., 2010; Carroll et al., 2009; Fang et al., 2015; Guo et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CENP-LN interacted specifically with CENP-A nucleosome core particles but not with H3 nucleosome core particles in solid phase binding assays.
source: When immobilized on solid phase and challenged with CENP-A or H3 nucleosome core particles (NCPs), CENP-LN interacted specifically with CENP-ANCP (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The CENP-A-binding region of the CENP-LN complex lies within the N-terminal region of CENP-N (residues 1-212).
source: As shown previously (Carroll et al., 2009), the CENP-A-binding region of the CENP-LN complex lies within the N-terminal region of CENP-N, because a stable fragment encompassing residues 1–212 of human CENP-N (CENP-N1-212) also bound selectively to CENP-ANCPs but not H3NCPs (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and a citation to previous work.

claim: The crystal structure of CENP-N1-235 was determined at 2.8 Å resolution.
source: We obtained well diffracting crystals of the CENP-N1-235 construct and determined its crystal structure at 2.8 Å resolution (Table 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding stated in the results.

claim: CENP-N1-235 consists of two closely juxtaposed domains that interact through an extended interface to form a single structural unit.
source: CENP-N1-235 consists of two closely juxtaposed domains that interact through an extended interface to form a single structural unit (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: The first domain of CENP-N1-235 (residues 1-77) consists of a five-helix bundle.
source: The first domain (residues 1–77) consists of a five-helix bundle, whereas the second domain (residues 78–212, cyan in Figure 1A) consists of a six-stranded anti-parallel β-sheet sandwiched between α-helices (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: The second domain of CENP-N1-235 (residues 78-212) consists of a six-stranded anti-parallel β-sheet sandwiched between α-helices.
source: The first domain (residues 1–77) consists of a five-helix bundle, whereas the second domain (residues 78–212, cyan in Figure 1A) consists of a six-stranded anti-parallel β-sheet sandwiched between α-helices (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: There is no clear density beyond residue ~210 in the CENP-N1-235 crystal structure, indicating that the structure is disordered after this point.
source: There is no clear density beyond residue ~210, indicating that the structure is disordered after this point.
evidence: This is an observation from the crystal structure stated in the results.

claim: The first domain of CENP-N shows similarity to PYRIN domains (PYDs) according to fold-recognition by DALI.
source: Fold-recognition by DALI (Holm and Rosenström, 2010) identified similarity of the first domain to PYRIN domains (PYDs; a superposition is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is a finding from computational analysis stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B.

claim: PYDs are 'death fold' family domains implicated in protein-protein interactions relevant to inflammation and apoptosis.
source: PYDs are 'death fold' family domains implicated in protein-protein interactions relevant to inflammation and apoptosis (Ratsimandresy et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: PYDs have not been previously implicated in interactions with DNA or chromatin.
source: They have not been previously implicated in interactions with DNA or chromatin.
evidence: This is stated in the results and represents knowledge from the literature.

claim: DALI identified an unanticipated structural homology of the second domain of CENP-N1-235 with the N-terminal domain of Iml3CENP-L.
source: Besides identifying the N-terminal domain of CENP-N1-235 as a PYRIN domain, DALI also identified an unanticipated structural homology of the second domain of CENP-N1-235 with the N-terminal domain of Iml3CENP-L (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from computational analysis stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The structurally similar domains of CENP-N and CENP-L are referred to as CLN-HD (for CENP-L and CENP-N homology domain).
source: We therefore refer to these domains of CENP-N and CENP-L as CLN-HD (for CENP-L and CENP-N homology domain).
evidence: This is stated in the results as a naming convention based on structural similarity.

claim: Structural similarities of the CLN-HD suggest that CENP-N and CENP-L are evolutionary related.
source: Structural similarities of the CLN-HD suggest that CENP-N and CENP-L are evolutionary related.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the results based on structural similarity.

claim: Sequence identity of the CLN-HD domains of CENP-N and CENP-L is minimal, even after structural superposition.
source: However, sequence identity of the two domains, even after structural superposition, is minimal, likely explaining why structural similarity had not been predicted (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This is an observation stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3D.

claim: CENP-L, or its complex with CENP-N230-C, did not interact with CENP-ANCPs or H3NCPs.
source: CENP-L, or its complex with CENP-N230-C, did not interact with CENP-ANCPs or H3NCPs (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: CENP-L and CENP-N, even if partly structurally related, have clearly distinct functions.
source: Thus, CENP-L and CENP-N, even if partly structurally related, have clearly distinct functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on experimental data showing differential binding properties.

claim: A three-dimensional reconstruction of CENP-N1-289 bound to CENP-ANCPs was obtained at ~4.0 Å resolution using cryo electron microscopy.
source: Using cryo electron microscopy (cryo-EM), we obtained a three-dimensional reconstruction of CENP-N1-289 bound to CENP-ANCPs at ~4.0 Å (Figure 3A–B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Table 2).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A–B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Table 2.

claim: Both manual and automatic fitting strategies produced unequivocal fits of the atomic model into the EM density.
source: Both manual and automatic fitting strategies produced unequivocal fits, allowing the first visualization of the interaction of CENP-N with the CENP-A nucleosome (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The CENP-A nucleosome appears to be stabilized by its interaction with CENP-N.
source: The CENP-A nucleosome appears to be stabilized by its interaction with CENP-N (Guo et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: There is clear density for 139 of the 147 bp of DNA in the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP complex structure.
source: There is clear density for 139 of the 147 bp of DNA and for the N-terminal helix of CENP-A (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), two features reported to be largely disordered and thus invisible in the crystal structure of the CENP-ANCP (PDB ID 3AN2) (Tachiwana et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: There is clear density for the N-terminal helix of CENP-A in the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP complex structure.
source: There is clear density for 139 of the 147 bp of DNA and for the N-terminal helix of CENP-A (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), two features reported to be largely disordered and thus invisible in the crystal structure of the CENP-ANCP (PDB ID 3AN2) (Tachiwana et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The DNA ends and N-terminal helix of CENP-A were reported to be largely disordered and invisible in the crystal structure of the CENP-ANCP.
source: There is clear density for 139 of the 147 bp of DNA and for the N-terminal helix of CENP-A (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), two features reported to be largely disordered and thus invisible in the crystal structure of the CENP-ANCP (PDB ID 3AN2) (Tachiwana et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The structure of CENP-N changes very little upon binding to the CENP-A nucleosome.
source: CENP-N, whose structure changes very little upon binding to the CENP-A nucleosome, is positioned on top of the L1 loop of CENP-A (also called RG loop for the presence of a conserved arginine-glycine motif at the loop's apex) and contacts approximately 15 base pairs of the adjacent DNA gyre (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the crystal structure and cryo-EM structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: CENP-N is positioned on top of the L1 loop of CENP-A and contacts approximately 15 base pairs of the adjacent DNA gyre.
source: CENP-N, whose structure changes very little upon binding to the CENP-A nucleosome, is positioned on top of the L1 loop of CENP-A (also called RG loop for the presence of a conserved arginine-glycine motif at the loop's apex) and contacts approximately 15 base pairs of the adjacent DNA gyre (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There is clear density only until CENP-N1-289 residue ~210 in the cryo-EM structure, indicating that the following approximately 80 C-terminal residues may be flexible.
source: There is clear density only until CENP-N1-289 residue ~210, indicating that the following approximately 80 C-terminal residues (at the opposite end of the nucleosome interaction interface) may be flexible.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results.

claim: Of the ~2400 Å2 of CENP-ANCP and CENP-N surface area that become buried in the complex, ~1400 Å2 are at the CENP-N:DNA interface.
source: Of the ~2400 Å2 of CENP-ANCP and CENP-N surface area that become buried in the complex,~1400 Å2 are at the CENP-N:DNA interface, where both CENP-N domains form extensive interactions with DNA from bp −21 to −35 relative to the twofold axis, or superhelical location [SHL] −2 to −3.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the cryo-EM structure stated in the results.

claim: Both CENP-N domains form extensive interactions with DNA from bp −21 to −35 relative to the twofold axis, or superhelical location [SHL] −2 to −3.
source: Of the ~2400 Å2 of CENP-ANCP and CENP-N surface area that become buried in the complex,~1400 Å2 are at the CENP-N:DNA interface, where both CENP-N domains form extensive interactions with DNA from bp −21 to −35 relative to the twofold axis, or superhelical location [SHL] −2 to −3.
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results.

claim: There is a marked accumulation of positively charged residues on the DNA binding interface of CENP-N.
source: There is a marked accumulation of positively charged residues on this DNA binding interface (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Four loops in the CLN-HD straddle the DNA double helix over ~8 bp.
source: Four loops in the CLN-HD straddle the DNA double helix over ~8 bp, and the consecutive 7 bp are bound by the PYRIN domain, which is positioned to insert an arginine (R44) into the compressed minor groove in an arrangement that is reminiscent of the minor groove arginines inserted by the histones (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The PYRIN domain is positioned to insert an arginine (R44) into the compressed minor groove in an arrangement that is reminiscent of the minor groove arginines inserted by the histones.
source: Four loops in the CLN-HD straddle the DNA double helix over ~8 bp, and the consecutive 7 bp are bound by the PYRIN domain, which is positioned to insert an arginine (R44) into the compressed minor groove in an arrangement that is reminiscent of the minor groove arginines inserted by the histones (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The highly conserved P17 in the PYRIN domain positions the main chain of CENP-N to latch on to the phosphate backbone of the DNA.
source: The highly conserved P17 in the PYRIN domain positions the main chain of CENP-N to latch on to the phosphate backbone of the DNA, with interactions made through the side chains of K15, R42, K45, K81, and R194.
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results.

claim: CENP-N side chains K15, R42, K45, K81, and R194 interact with the phosphate backbone of the DNA.
source: The highly conserved P17 in the PYRIN domain positions the main chain of CENP-N to latch on to the phosphate backbone of the DNA, with interactions made through the side chains of K15, R42, K45, K81, and R194.
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results.

claim: There are likely insertions of CENP-N side chains into two minor grooves (K148, M167, R170) and the intervening major groove at SHL −3 (R196).
source: There are also likely insertions of CENP-N side chains into two minor grooves (besides R44, also K148, M167, R170) and the intervening major groove at SHL −3 [R196, see also (Carroll et al., 2009) (Figure 3E)].
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results, shown in Figure 3E, and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: CENP-N bound more tightly to CENP-ANCPs but retained substantial binding affinity for H3NCPs in electrophoretic mobility shift assays.
source: In agreement with the presence of a large interaction interface with nucleosomal DNA, CENP-N bound more tightly to CENP-ANCPs but retained substantial binding affinity for H3NCPs in electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–B.

claim: The residual binding of CENP-N to H3NCPs in EMSAs likely reflects emphasis on electrostatic interactions under the low-salt conditions of the EMSA assays.
source: Likely, this residual binding to H3NCPs in the EMSAs, which emerged less clearly in solid phase binding assays (Figure 1C), reflects emphasis on electrostatic interactions under the low-salt conditions of the EMSA assays (150 mM NaCl for complex formation, followed by further dilution upon loading onto the gel), compared to the GST-binding assays (300 mM NaCl), as also discussed in the context of Figure 4—figure supplement 2.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on experimental observations.

claim: The substantial interface with DNA explains why CENP-N does not bind CENP-A:H4 tetramers lacking DNA.
source: The substantial interface with DNA explains why CENP-N does not bind CENP-A:H4 tetramers lacking DNA (Carroll et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the structural data and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: DNA binding contributes to the binding affinity of the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP interaction but is unlikely to contribute to the discrimination of CENP-ANCPs from H3NCPs.
source: However, while DNA binding clearly contributes to the binding affinity of this interaction, it is unlikely to contribute to the discrimination of CENP-ANCPs from H3NCPs, because CENP-N bound selectively to CENP-ANCPs even when the CENP-ANCPs and H3NCPs contained the same DNA sequence (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B–C.

claim: Recognition of the L1 loop is crucial for discrimination of CENP-ANCPs from H3NCPs by CENP-N.
source: Conversely, the structure clearly suggests why recognition of the L1 loop is crucial for discrimination (Black et al., 2004; Carroll et al., 2010, 2009).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on the structural data and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CENP-N binds the L1 loop through a continuous interface comprising the α1 helix in CENP-NPD and the β3-β4 loop in CENP-NCLN-HD.
source: CENP-N binds the L1 loop through a continuous interface comprising the α1 helix in CENP-NPD and the β3-β4 loop in CENP-NCLN-HD.
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results.

claim: Several of the infrequent conserved solvent-exposed residues of CENP-N, including E3, E7, R11, K143, P145, N146, and K148, reside in the L1 loop binding interface.
source: Several of the infrequent conserved solvent-exposed residues of CENP-N (identified by a green dot in Figure 2D), including E3, E7, R11, K143, P145, N146, and K148 reside in this interface.
evidence: This is an observation from the structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Y147 of CENP-N contributes to the stabilization of the relative arrangements of the CENP-NPD and CENP-NCLN-HD.
source: Y147, which is less conserved, contributes to the stabilization of the relative arrangements of the CENP-NPD and CENP-NCLN-HD, which is largely unchanged in the nucleosome-bound and free structures of CENP-N.
evidence: This is an observation from the structure stated in the results.

claim: Insertion of the side chain of M1 into the hydrophobic core contributes to the stabilization of the α1 helix of CENP-N.
source: Insertion of the side chain of M1 into the hydrophobic core contributes to the stabilization of the α1 helix.
evidence: This is an observation from the structure stated in the results.

claim: The interaction with the CENP-A L1 loop engages a triad of residues, E3CENP-N, E7CENP-N, and R11CENP-N, whose side chains emerge from the same face of the α1 helix looking toward the L1 loop.
source: The interaction with the CENP-A L1 loop engages a triad of residues, E3CENP-N, E7CENP-N, and R11CENP-N, whose side chains emerge from the same face of the α1 helix looking toward the L1 loop (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The CENP-A residues R80CENP-A and G81CENP-A form a two-residue insertion that is the most conspicuous difference between the L1 loops in CENP-A and H3.
source: The CENP-A residues R80CENP-A and G81CENP-A form a two-residue insertion that is the most conspicuous difference between the L1 loops in CENP-A and H3 (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 4A–B).
evidence: This is an observation from the structure stated in the results and shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 4A–B.

claim: The R80-G81 insertion is crucial because it allows R80CENP-A to form hydrogen bonds with both E3CENP-N and E7CENP-N.
source: The insertion is crucial, because it allows R80CENP-A to form hydrogen bonds with both E3CENP-N and E7CENP-N, while absence of a side chain at G81CENP-A allows the CENP-A loop to insert deeply into a cleft formed between the two CENP-N domains, where the side chain of Y147CENP-N packs tightly against V82CENP-A.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data stated in the results.

claim: Absence of a side chain at G81CENP-A allows the CENP-A loop to insert deeply into a cleft formed between the two CENP-N domains, where the side chain of Y147CENP-N packs tightly against V82CENP-A.
source: The insertion is crucial, because it allows R80CENP-A to form hydrogen bonds with both E3CENP-N and E7CENP-N, while absence of a side chain at G81CENP-A allows the CENP-A loop to insert deeply into a cleft formed between the two CENP-N domains, where the side chain of Y147CENP-N packs tightly against V82CENP-A.
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results.

claim: Mutation of R80 and G81 to alanine partly ablated the preference of CENP-N for CENP-ANCPs in EMSAs.
source: In EMSAs, mutation of R80 and G81 to alanine partly ablated the preference of CENP-N for CENP-ANCPs (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A–B.

claim: The side chain of R11CENP-N is squeezed between the loop 1 region of CENP-A and the loop 2 region of H4, where it may be involved in a double salt bridge with E74H4 and E7CENP-N.
source: The side chain of R11CENP-N, a residue previously shown to be important for the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP interaction (Carroll et al., 2009), on the other hand, is squeezed between the loop 1 region of CENP-A and the loop 2 region of H4, where it may be involved in a double salt bridge with E74H4 and E7CENP-N (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the cryo-EM structure stated in the results, shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 5, and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: R11 was previously shown to be important for the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP interaction.
source: The side chain of R11CENP-N, a residue previously shown to be important for the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP interaction (Carroll et al., 2009), on the other hand, is squeezed between the loop 1 region of CENP-A and the loop 2 region of H4, where it may be involved in a double salt bridge with E74H4 and E7CENP-N (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: An alanine mutant of R11 showed essentially complete loss of binding to CENP-ANCPs in pull-down assays in vitro.
source: In pull-down assays in vitro, we found essentially complete loss of binding with an alanine (A) mutant of R11 (Figure 4A), and substantial reductions of binding with alanine mutants of E7 or Y147, at the CENP-A L1 interface, or of K15 or K45, at the interface with DNA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Alanine mutants of E7 or Y147 (at the CENP-A L1 interface) or of K15 or K45 (at the interface with DNA) showed substantial reductions of binding to CENP-ANCPs in pull-down assays in vitro.
source: In pull-down assays in vitro, we found essentially complete loss of binding with an alanine (A) mutant of R11 (Figure 4A), and substantial reductions of binding with alanine mutants of E7 or Y147, at the CENP-A L1 interface, or of K15 or K45, at the interface with DNA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Combining mutations of Y147 with either K15 or K45 almost completely disrupted CENP-ANCP binding.
source: Combining mutations of Y147 with either K15 or K45 almost completely disrupted CENP-ANCP binding (Figure 4A), in line with the idea that recognition of the L1 loop and of the DNA jointly contribute to the binding affinity of CENP-N for the CENP-A nucleosome.
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Recognition of the L1 loop and of the DNA jointly contribute to the binding affinity of CENP-N for the CENP-A nucleosome.
source: Combining mutations of Y147 with either K15 or K45 almost completely disrupted CENP-ANCP binding (Figure 4A), in line with the idea that recognition of the L1 loop and of the DNA jointly contribute to the binding affinity of CENP-N for the CENP-A nucleosome.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on mutational data.

claim: CENP-N targeting to centromeres in U2OS cells reflected the observations made in vitro, with R11A single mutant and the K15A-Y147A and K45-Y147A double mutants appearing severely impaired in the ability to target centromeres.
source: CENP-N targeting to centromeres in U2OS cells reflected the observations made in vitro, with R11A single mutant and the K15A-Y147A and K45-Y147A double mutants appearing severely impaired in the ability to target centromeres (Figure 4B–C), and other single mutants suffering intermediate effects on binding to centromeres (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B–C.

claim: Other single mutants of CENP-N suffered intermediate effects on binding to centromeres in U2OS cells.
source: CENP-N targeting to centromeres in U2OS cells reflected the observations made in vitro, with R11A single mutant and the K15A-Y147A and K45-Y147A double mutants appearing severely impaired in the ability to target centromeres (Figure 4B–C), and other single mutants suffering intermediate effects on binding to centromeres (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CENP-N mutants at the CENP-A L1 loop interface lost the ability of CENP-Nwt to discriminate between CENP-A and H3-nucleosomes in competition gel shift assays.
source: In competition gel shift assays, CENP-N mutants at the CENP-A L1 loop interface (L1 mutants), including R11A and two double mutants (E3A-E7A and K143A-Y147A), lost the ability of CENP-Nwt to discriminate between CENP-A and H3-nucleosomes (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: The residual interaction of CENP-NR11A with CENP-ANCPs or H3NCPs in EMSAs likely reflects the extensive binding interface of CENP-N for nucleosomal DNA.
source: We have shown in Figure 4A that CENP-NR11A does not bind CENP-ANCPs in solid phase-binding assays. The residual interaction of this mutant with CENP-ANCPs or H3NCPs in EMSAs likely reflects the extensive binding interface of CENP-N for nucleosomal DNA (whose effects are emphasized under low-salt conditions, as already indicated for CENP-Nwt in the context of Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on experimental observations.

claim: In EMSAs, the L1 mutants of CENP-N bind H3NCPs indistinguishably from CENP-Nwt, whereas the same mutants bind to CENP-ANCPs considerably worse than CENP-Nwt.
source: In line with this interpretation, we find that in the EMSAs the L1 mutants of CENP-N bind H3NCPs indistinguishably from CENP-Nwt, whereas the same mutants bind to CENP-ANCPs considerably worse than CENP-Nwt (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: CENP-C2-545 binds the CENP-LN complex in vitro.
source: Within this assembly, CENP-C2-545 binds the CENP-LN complex in vitro [Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and (Hinshaw and Harrison, 2013; McKinley et al., 2015; Nagpal et al., 2015; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and citations to previous work.

claim: CENP-C225-364 is a minimal CENP-LN interaction domain.
source: Trimming of CENP-C2-545 identified CENP-C225-364 as a minimal CENP-LN interaction domain (Figure 5A), in line with a recent study (Guo et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results, shown in Figure 5A, and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Neither CENP-L nor CENP-N1-235 bound to CENP-C2-545.
source: Neither CENP-L nor CENP-N1-235 bound to CENP-C2-545 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B–C.

claim: The CENP-LN230-C dimer bound CENP-C in the absence of nucleosomes.
source: However, the CENP-LN230-C dimer bound CENP-C in the absence of nucleosomes (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: CENP-C225-364 binds at or near the CENP-LN dimer interface, possibly also exploiting structural ordering of these regions upon dimerization.
source: Thus, CENP-C225-364 binds at or near the CENP-LN dimer interface, possibly also exploiting structural ordering of these regions upon dimerization.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results based on experimental data.

claim: A 5-alanine mutant of residues 302–306 of CENP-C (identified as CENP-C5A) failed to interact with CENP-NL, identifying this region of CENP-C as the CENP-LN binding motif.
source: We probed an additional conserved linear motif in CENP-C225-364 (residues 302–306) for its potential role in CENP-N binding. A 5-alanine mutant of residues 302–306 (identified as CENP-C5A) failed to interact with CENP-NL, identifying this region of CENP-C as the CENP-LN binding motif (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: CENP-C2-545-5A did not interact with CENP-LN, but retained binding to CENP-ANCPs and CENP-HIKM.
source: Importantly, CENP-C2-545-5A did not interact with CENP-LN, but retained binding to CENP-ANCPs and CENP-HIKM (Figure 5E–F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 5E–F.

claim: CENP-LN230-C bound CENP-C225-364 with a dissociation constant (KD) of 1 µM in isothermal titration calorimetry experiments.
source: In isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments, CENP-LN230-C bound CENP-C225-364 with a dissociation constant (KD) of 1 µM, but it showed no binding to CENP-C225-364-5A (Figure 5G–H).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 5G–H.

claim: CENP-LN230-C showed no binding to CENP-C225-364-5A in isothermal titration calorimetry experiments.
source: In isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments, CENP-LN230-C bound CENP-C225-364 with a dissociation constant (KD) of 1 µM, but it showed no binding to CENP-C225-364-5A (Figure 5G–H).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 5G–H.

claim: Depletion of CENP-C prevented kinetochore localization of CENP-N, showing that nucleosome binding is not sufficient for CENP-N to reach kinetochores at the low cellular concentration of these proteins.
source: Depletion of CENP-C prevented kinetochore localization of CENP-N, showing that nucleosome binding is not sufficient for CENP-N to reach kinetochores at the low cellular concentration of these proteins.
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results.

claim: Exogenously expressed wild-type CENP-C promoted CENP-N recruitment to kinetochores, while CENP-C5A failed to promote it.
source: Exogenously expressed wild-type CENP-C promoted CENP-N recruitment, while CENP-C5A failed to promote it (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding stated in the results and shown in Figure 6A–B.

claim: The CENP-LN binding site of CENP-C is crucial for CENP-N recruitment to kinetochores, but not for CENP-C recruitment to kinetochores.
source: Thus, the CENP-LN binding site of CENP-C, while not crucial for CENP-C recruitment to kinetochores, is instead crucial for CENP-N recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on experimental data.

claim: The CENP-LN complex reads the presence of two features of kinetochores, the presence of CENP-A and the presence of CENP-C, both of which are necessary for its efficient recruitment.
source: Overall, these observations indicate that the CENP-LN complex reads the presence of two features of kinetochores, the presence of CENP-A and the presence of CENP-C, both of which are necessary for its efficient recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results based on experimental data.

claim: CENP-N nucleosome binding differs from that observed with RCC1 and other nucleosome binders that engage primarily an exposed acidic patch on histones H2A and H2B.
source: CENP-N nucleosome binding differs from that observed with RCC1 and other nucleosome binders that engage primarily an exposed acidic patch on histones H2A and H2B (Makde et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In its outline, CENP-N binding resembles the interaction of the ATPase domain of SWI2/SNF2 chromatin remodeler with H3NCPs.
source: However, in its outline it resembles the interaction of the ATPase domain of SWI2/SNF2 chromatin remodeler with H3NCPs (Farnung et al., 2017; Liu et al., 2017; Narlikar et al., 2013), with the important difference that SWI2/SNF2 closely approaches H3 without making significant direct contacts with it, whereas CENP-N interacts directly with CENP-A (Figure 3—figure supplement 6A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion, supported by citations to previous work, and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6A–D.

claim: SWI2/SNF2 closely approaches H3 without making significant direct contacts with it, whereas CENP-N interacts directly with CENP-A.
source: However, in its outline it resembles the interaction of the ATPase domain of SWI2/SNF2 chromatin remodeler with H3NCPs (Farnung et al., 2017; Liu et al., 2017; Narlikar et al., 2013), with the important difference that SWI2/SNF2 closely approaches H3 without making significant direct contacts with it, whereas CENP-N interacts directly with CENP-A (Figure 3—figure supplement 6A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion, supported by citations to previous work, and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6A–D.

claim: There are similarities between CENP-N binding and the nucleosome-binding mechanism of the bromo-adjacent homology (BAH) domain of Sir3.
source: There are also similarities with the nucleosome-binding mechanism of the bromo-adjacent homology (BAH) domain of Sir3 (PDB ID 3TU4) (Armache et al., 2011), but the latter interacts predominantly with the H4 N-terminal tail, through recognition of K16H4, and with the acidic patch on H2A-H2B, and much less extensively with DNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 6E–F).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion, supported by a citation to previous work, and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6E–F.

claim: The BAH domain of Sir3 interacts predominantly with the H4 N-terminal tail, through recognition of K16H4, and with the acidic patch on H2A-H2B, and much less extensively with DNA.
source: There are also similarities with the nucleosome-binding mechanism of the bromo-adjacent homology (BAH) domain of Sir3 (PDB ID 3TU4) (Armache et al., 2011), but the latter interacts predominantly with the H4 N-terminal tail, through recognition of K16H4, and with the acidic patch on H2A-H2B, and much less extensively with DNA (Figure 3—figure supplement 6E–F).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion, supported by a citation to previous work, and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6E–F.

claim: In the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP complex, the normally disordered N-terminal tail of H4 is ordered until R23 and interacts weakly with the CENP-N loop connecting β3 with β4.
source: In the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP complex, the normally disordered N-terminal tail of H4 is ordered until R23 and interacts weakly with the CENP-N loop connecting β3 with β4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The reported mono-methylation of K20 of H4 in the CENP-A nucleosome may further modulate the interaction with CENP-N.
source: The reported mono-methylation of K20 of H4 in the CENP-A nucleosome (Hori et al., 2014) may further modulate this interaction.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on a citation to previous work.

claim: The SWI2/SNF2 and BAH modes of nucleosome binding are predominantly based on interactions with DNA or with the histones, respectively, while CENP-N shows a balance of both.
source: In summary, the SWI2/SNF2 and BAH modes of nucleosome binding are predominantly based on interactions with DNA or with the histones, respectively, while CENP-N shows a balance of both.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the discussion based on structural comparisons.

claim: The considerable interaction of CENP-N with DNA is a remarkable and unexpected feature of the complex structure.
source: The considerable interaction of CENP-N with DNA is a remarkable and unexpected feature of the complex structure.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: CENP-C and CENP-N can interact concomitantly with the same CENP-A nucleosome.
source: CENP-C and CENP-N can interact concomitantly with the same CENP-A nucleosome (Carroll et al., 2010), as also confirmed in recent studies (Guo et al., 2017; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The determinants of CENP-C binding on CENP-A are located adjacent to, but not overlapping with, the CENP-N-binding footprint.
source: These determinants of CENP-C binding on CENP-A are located adjacent to, but not overlapping with, the CENP-N-binding footprint.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on structural analysis.

claim: When modeled on the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP structure according to the position it adopts in its structure with the nucleosome, the CENP-C motif can be accommodated without steric clashes.
source: Indeed, when modeled on the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP structure according to the position it adopts in its structure with the nucleosome (PDB ID 4 × 23) (Kato et al., 2013), the CENP-C motif can be accommodated without steric clashes (Figure 6C,E).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion, supported by a citation to previous work, and shown in Figure 6C,E.

claim: CENP-C and CENP-N interact with CENP-A through complementary interfaces.
source: Thus, CENP-C and CENP-N interact with CENP-A through complementary interfaces.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on structural analysis.

claim: In the context of a larger CCAN complex, the CENP-A-binding motifs of CENP-C and CENP-N cooperate to increase the overall binding affinity for CENP-A.
source: In the context of a larger CCAN complex, these CENP-A-binding motifs cooperate to increase the overall binding affinity for CENP-A (Guo et al., 2017; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: It has been proposed that CENP-N is significantly stabilized upon binding to the CENP-A nucleosome.
source: It has been proposed that CENP-N is significantly stabilized upon binding to the CENP-A nucleosome (Guo et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The study did not identify a clear structural basis for the stabilization of CENP-N upon binding to the CENP-A nucleosome, as no significant conformational changes in CENP-N were observed.
source: Our study did not identify a clear structural basis for this phenomenon, as we failed to identify significant conformational changes in CENP-N in isolation (crystal structure) compared to its complex with CENP-ANCP.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on structural comparisons.

claim: It has been proposed that CENP-C reshapes and rigidifies the CENP-A nucleosome and that it modulates the DNA termini to make them match the loose wrap observed at centromeres.
source: It has also been proposed that CENP-C reshapes and rigidifies the CENP-A nucleosome and that it modulates the DNA termini to make them match the loose wrap observed at centromeres (Falk et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The effects of CENP-C binding on the CENP-A nucleosome do not appear to be required for the selective (over H3) interaction of CENP-N.
source: Importantly, these effects of CENP-C binding on the CENP-A nucleosome do not appear to be required for the selective (over H3) interaction of CENP-N, because selectivity for CENP-A was retained in the absence of CENP-C [this study and (Carroll et al., 2009; Weir et al., 2016)].
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by experimental data from this study and citations to previous work.

claim: The DNA termini appear to be well defined in the structure of the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP complex, contrarily to what was observed in the structure of the isolated CENP-ANCP.
source: We also note that the DNA termini appear to be well defined in our structure of the CENP-N:CENP-ANCP complex, contrarily to what was observed in the structure of the isolated CENP-ANCP (PDB ID 3AN2).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on structural observations.

claim: It is possible that the stabilization of the DNA termini is due to CENP-N binding to the CENP-A nucleosome.
source: At present, we cannot definitively conclude whether the stabilization of the termini is due to CENP-N binding to the CENP-A nucleosome, as we have not yet been able to obtain a high-resolution EM structure of the CENP-A nucleosome in isolation for comparison.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on structural observations.

claim: It is possible that the cryogenic conditions used for the structural work stabilize a specific conformation of the complex.
source: It is possible that the cryogenic conditions used for our structural work stabilize a specific conformation of the complex.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: In most organisms, centromere identity is not specified by the centromere's DNA sequence, but rather by the enrichment of CENP-A at a defined chromatin domain.
source: In most organisms, centromere identity is not specified by the centromere's DNA sequence, but rather by the enrichment of CENP-A at a defined chromatin domain.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents established knowledge about centromere specification.

claim: De novo formation of stably inherited centromeres at previously non-centromeric sites (neo-centromeres) provides clear evidence that centromeres are epigenetically specified.
source: De novo formation of stably inherited centromeres at previously non-centromeric sites (neo-centromeres) provides clear evidence in favor of this idea.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents established knowledge about centromere specification.

claim: Centromeres are epigenetically specified, with the pre-existing enrichment of CENP-A being a necessary condition for continued deposition of new CENP-A at the same site through the generations.
source: Thus, rather than being genetically (i.e. DNA-sequence) specified, centromeres are epigenetically specified, with the pre-existing enrichment of CENP-A being a necessary condition for continued deposition of new CENP-A at the same site through the generations.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and represents established knowledge about centromere specification.

claim: Conserved machinery for new CENP-A deposition includes the specialized CENP-A chaperone HJURP (Scm3 in S. cerevisiae) and an adaptor complex consisting of the Mis18 and M18BP1 subunits.
source: Conserved machinery for new CENP-A deposition, including the specialized CENP-A chaperone HJURP (Scm3 in S. cerevisiae) and an adaptor complex consisting of the Mis18 and M18BP1 subunits, has been described in recent years (Dunleavy et al., 2009; Foltz et al., 2009; Fujita et al., 2007; Hayashi et al., 2004; Pidoux et al., 2009; Sanchez-Pulido et al., 2009; Williams et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Additional machinery, in particular chromatin remodelling enzymes harnessing ATP hydrolysis to evict H3, is likely involved in CENP-A deposition but has not been univocally identified.
source: Additional machinery, in particular chromatin remodelling enzymes harnessing ATP hydrolysis to evict H3, is likely involved in the reaction but has not been univocally identified.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on knowledge of the field.

claim: The CENP-A deposition machinery is recruited to centromeres early during the cell-cycle and is believed to promote the replacement of histone H3 with new CENP-A.
source: This machinery is recruited to centromeres early during the cell-cycle and is believed to promote the replacement of histone H3 with new CENP-A (Dunleavy et al., 2011; Jansen et al., 2007; Schuh et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The existing CENP-A nucleosome likely acts as a template in the CENP-A deposition reaction.
source: Likely, the existing CENP-A nucleosome acts as a template in this reaction, as the abundance of CENP-A nucleosomes at a given centromere is, at least in first approximation, constant through subsequent cell divisions (French et al., 2017; Hori et al., 2017; Jansen et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as inference supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The abundance of CENP-A nucleosomes at a given centromere is, at least in first approximation, constant through subsequent cell divisions.
source: Likely, the existing CENP-A nucleosome acts as a template in this reaction, as the abundance of CENP-A nucleosomes at a given centromere is, at least in first approximation, constant through subsequent cell divisions (French et al., 2017; Hori et al., 2017; Jansen et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The same number of new CENP-A nucleosomes is incorporated after each cell division as that of originally present CENP-A nucleosomes.
source: This implies that the same number of new CENP-A nucleosomes is incorporated after each cell division as that of originally present CENP-A nucleosomes, suggesting that the deposition machinery targets, for H3 eviction and replacement with CENP-A, an H3 nucleosome that is likely in close proximity of the CENP-A nucleosome (Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as inference supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The deposition machinery targets, for H3 eviction and replacement with CENP-A, an H3 nucleosome that is likely in close proximity of the CENP-A nucleosome.
source: This implies that the same number of new CENP-A nucleosomes is incorporated after each cell division as that of originally present CENP-A nucleosomes, suggesting that the deposition machinery targets, for H3 eviction and replacement with CENP-A, an H3 nucleosome that is likely in close proximity of the CENP-A nucleosome (Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as inference supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Recruitment of the CENP-A deposition machinery requires CENP-C and possibly other CCAN factors.
